Singapore’s Meridian Bank Enters Administration Amid Mounting Losses

Singapore, June 17, 2024 – Meridian Bank, a mid-sized lender with a significant retail and corporate presence in Singapore, entered court-appointed administration on Monday following months of deteriorating balance sheets and unsuccessful attempts to secure additional capital. The move marks the most high-profile insolvency in the city-state’s banking industry in over a decade.

The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) confirmed that Meridian Bank has been placed under the control of administrators from a local restructuring firm, citing concerns over the bank’s ability to meet its obligations to depositors and creditors. Operations at Meridian’s 23 branches across Singapore have been severely curtailed, with customer withdrawals and new lending activities temporarily suspended as the administrators begin an urgent assessment of the bank’s financial position.

“Meridian Bank’s entry into administration is a regrettable but necessary step to protect the interests of its customers and maintain confidence in Singapore’s banking sector,” said MAS spokesperson Rachel Lim at a press briefing. “Our immediate priority is to ensure the orderly management of the bank’s assets and liabilities while safeguarding the stability of the financial system.”

Meridian Bank’s collapse follows a sharp rise in non-performing loans in its corporate lending portfolio, with sources close to the bank indicating that bad debts have more than doubled over the past year. The bank reported a full-year loss of S$412 million for 2023, compared to a profit of S$86 million the previous year. Efforts to raise fresh equity from investors or pursue a merger with a domestic rival failed to materialize in recent weeks.

According to an internal memo seen by reporters, the bank’s staff of 1,400 have been told to report for duty as usual but have been assured that salaries for June will be paid. “We are committed to supporting our employees during this challenging time,” interim CEO Darren Cheong wrote. “Further updates regarding job security and the future of Meridian Bank will be communicated as soon as possible.”

The Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS) said in a statement that it is closely monitoring the situation and is in contact with the administrators to ensure that customers’ interests are protected. Analysts note that while the administration of Meridian Bank is a significant event for the local banking industry, Singapore’s regulatory framework and deposit insurance scheme are expected to limit broader financial fallout.

At the time of writing, the administrators are conducting a comprehensive review of Meridian Bank’s loan book and asset quality, with further updates anticipated in the coming days. The MAS has urged customers to remain calm as the process continues.
